thread.title: Stocks Rumble Higher: Netflix Leads FANG Bounce, Big Banks Mixed | Investor's Business Daily

author: ALAN R. ELLIOTT
title: Stocks Rumble Higher: Netflix Leads FANG Bounce, Big Banks Mixed | Investor's Business Daily
text:
Stocks launched into a broad bounce at Friday's open as the market moved to grab back a piece of the week's heavy losses.
X Netflix ( NFLX ) surged in early action after a flurry of analyst actions. Chip makers rallied, with Advanced Micro Devices ( AMD ) and Nvidia ( NVDA ) staking out early leads. China-based leaders took a powerful bounce, with Tencent Holdings ( TCEHY ), NetEase ( NTES ), JD.com ( JD ) and Alibaba Group ( BABA ) rising more than 3%.
Big banks JPMorgan ( JPM ), Citigroup ( C ) and Wells Fargo ( WFC ) rallied on the release of their third-quarter results. PNC Financial ( PNC ) lost ground following its report.
The Nasdaq Composite kicked 2.2% higher at the start of trade. China-based Ctrip.com ( CTRP ) and Nvidia headed up the early advance. All 100 stocks traded flat or higher.
The Dow Jones industrial average jumped 1.5%, as more than half of the index posted early gains of more than 1%. Visa ( VISA ) and Apple ( AAPL ) muscled up 3.8% and 2.7%, respectively. The S&P 500 also vaulted 1.5%, with Alaska Air Group ( ALK ) and Nvidia pacing the index's early gains.
A volatile stretch for the market has seen the Dow and Nasdaq each decline in five of the past six sessions. The S&P 500 dropped for five straight days. The result sends the Dow into Friday's session down 5.3% for the week, fractionally below its 200-day moving average and testing support at that line.
The Nasdaq and S&P 500 are down 5.9% and 5.5%, respectively. Both have broken well below their 200-day lines.
Hong Kong, South Korea, India Lead Global Rebound Markets across Asia bounced Friday, buoyed by strong export and trade surplus data from China. Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index leapt 2.1%, but ended down 2.9% for the week in a second straight weekly dive and still deep in bear-market terrain. The Shanghai Composite climbed 0.9%. That eased the index's loss for the week to 0.8%, also still deep in bear-market status.
Markets in South Korea and India also surged, with Seoul's Kospi Index up 1.6% and the Bombay Stock Exchange's Sensex rising 2.2%.
In Japan, Tokyo's Nikkei 225 climbed 0.5%, rebounding from its 200-day level and narrowing its loss for the week to 4.6% — the index's worst drop since March.
European markets added to their early gains in afternoon trade. London's FTSE 100 swung 0.7% higher. The CAC-40 in Paris gained 0.8%. Frankfurt's DAX climbed 0.7%.
Netflix Paces Early Surge; Citigroup Leads Big Banks Netflix opened 4.4% higher as the stock aimed to retake support at its 200-day moving average. Shares dropped 8.6% for the week through Thursday, stopping well short of the August low in the current four-month consolidation.
Stifel Nicolaus reiterated its buy rating on Netflix, but trimmed the stock's price target to 395, from 406. A Citigroup note advised investors to buy on the dip, upgraded the stock to buy from neutral and reiterated its 375 price target. Netflix reports third-quarter results on Tuesday.
Amazon.com ( AMZN ) scrambled ahead 3.9%, the second-strongest move among its FANG stock tech peers.
JPMorgan pared its opening gain to 0.7% after kicking off the third-quarter reporting season for big banks. It turned in earnings and revenue that were above forecasts. Higher interest rates helped results, though home lending revenue fell . Shares are looking to recoup some of the week's 5.7% decline through Thursday, and retake their converged 10- and 40-week lines of support. The stock has been consolidating since March.
Citigroup rallied 3.3% as earnings rose more than forecast, while revenue slipped 0.2%, more than expected by analyst consensus. A 21% tax decrease and a sharp drop in cost apparently cheered investors. The stock is trading below a 75.34 buy point in a saucer with handle base, although investors should not be buying stocks while the market is in a correction .
Wells Fargo tightened its early gain to 1%. PNC Financial dropped 3.6% as third-quarter earnings and revenue met or topped analysts' targets, but residential mortgage revenue dropped 27%.
IBD 50 Stocks: Match Gets Buy Rating, Abiomed Soars Abiomed ( ABMD ) and TradeDesk ( TTD ) jumped to the lead among IBD 50 stocks .
Abiomed rebounded 7.5%, enough to reverse losses and put the stock on positive ground for the week. Abiomed had earlier tripped the automatic sell rule , falling more than 8% below a 451.03 buy point.
Match Group ( MTCH ) spiked 5% after falling 8.2% for the week through Thursday. Instinet initiated coverage on the stock with a buy rating and a 66 price target. The stock had pulled back to retest a buy point at 48.75. In the process, it gave up a 25% gain and cut below its 10-week moving average in heavy trade. Both are sell signals .
Econ News: September Import Prices Jump, Exports Flat Import prices jumped 0.5% in September, the Labor Department reported, a sharp reversal from August's 0.6% decline and more than double consensus views for a 0.2% rise. Export prices were flat, after a 0.1% slip in August, and vs. forecasts for a 0.2% decline.
Year-over-year, import price growth slowed to 3.5%, from 3.7%. Export price growth dropped sharply, to 2.7% from a 3.6% advance in August.
A preliminary reading on October consumer sentiment is expected from the University of Michigan at 10 a.m. ET. The Treasury Department is scheduled to release its September budget numbers at 2 p.m. ET.
Oil traded higher Friday but down sharply for the week. West Texas Intermediate added 0.4% to $71.38 per barrel. That left the benchmark down 4% for the week, track toward its worst weekly loss since May. The weekly oil rig count from BakerHughes ( BHGE ) is set for release at 1 p.m. ET.
